content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows upward trend bias, often overshooting recent highs or missing sharp downward corrections.
- After a price spike, model continues rising too aggressively, failing to recognize mean reversion or volatility decay.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward moves in the latter half of the 30-day window, particularly after mid-range peaks.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, leading to over-optimistic upward forecasts when prices are consolidating or declining.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds onto upward bias even after price drops, ignoring momentum reversal.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if recent 7–14 day average is below 80.00, especially if true price is falling below 80.00.
- If true price drops below 75.00 after a spike above 85.00, model should reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to reflect volatility decay.
- Model should not extrapolate upward beyond 85.00 unless confirmed by 3 consecutive days of price stability above 85.00.
